question: Does Rumble Scrapper equipped with Skyfall of Areion while conquering with a Blue Sentinel play 2 mech tokens?
answer:
No — still 1 Mech token. Skyfall of Areion only widens which event satisfies Rumble's "When I hold" condition; it doesn't make the trigger something Blue Sentinel can add to, and a single Conquer is a single trigger (FAQ #9733).

Blue Sentinel's passive is scoped to "your hold effects for holding here" — it modifies triggers that happen because you held at that battlefield. Conquer and Hold are separate scoring methods (CR 471), and Skyfall doesn't convert your Conquer into a Hold (FAQ #5622: it adds legality for both events, it doesn't duplicate). So when Rumble conquers, his hold-effect-turned-conquer-effect triggers once, and Blue Sentinel adds nothing.

For contrast: if Rumble (with Skyfall) were present at that battlefield and you actually held it with Blue Sentinel there, the hold trigger would fire twice (2 tokens). question: heal after showdown
answer:
It depends on whether the showdown was a combat showdown — those heal all units; non-combat showdowns heal nothing.

If units controlled by different players were both present (a real combat), the Combat Cleanup during the Resolution Step heals all damage off every unit in play at once — including units sitting at Base or at other battlefields that never fought (CR 468.1.a.1, 463). But a non-combat showdown (you move to a battlefield and no enemy units are there) has no combat damage step and no Combat Cleanup, so damaged units just stay damaged (FAQ #9726, #11213).

Either way, all damage is also cleared for all units at end of turn during the Expiration Step (Rule 317.2.b). Note that healing only clears damage marks — it doesn't remove Might buffs or counters.

question: Can I react to dazzling aurora trigger with a temporal breach on disarming rake to kill the dazzling aurora? Will this stop the dazzling aurora trigger from happening
answer:
Yes to the play, no to the stop. You can absolutely react to Aurora's end-of-turn trigger, and Temporal Breach on your own Disarming Rake is a legal way to kill the Aurora — but the Aurora trigger still resolves and plays a unit.

The trigger is a finalized chain item in a Closed State, so only Reaction-speed things are legal; Hidden covers that (Temporal Breach hid earlier, so it's playable for [0]). Note it's the replayed Rake doing the killing, not the Breach — Breach banishes a unit, so the Rake re-enters and its "when you play me, you may kill a gear" trigger goes on the chain above Temporal Breach, killing the Aurora first.

Killing Aurora doesn't matter, though: effects already finalized on the chain always resolve unless countered, and Aurora's effect doesn't need its source on the board (FAQ 6408). To actually stop it you need something that counters the trigger itself or something that prevents a player from playing units.

The catch is the condition still has to actually happen. Hold only occurs during your own Beginning Phase, so on an opponent's turn the only possible trigger is a Conquer — and that does happen if, say, they Charm your unit into an empty battlefield: you take control there and score the conquer point even on their turn (FAQ #8299, #3426).

Her trigger still goes on the chain while she's exhausted (FAQ #604), but you can't finalize it if you can't pay the exhaust (CR 415.4, 423.3). Repulse is a Reaction, so you can play it while the trigger is on the chain, and countering clears the ability so nothing dies (CR 426.1.a).

The catch is Repulse's own target: it must choose a friendly unit at a battlefield. Harnessed Dragon has no location restriction and can kill a unit sitting in your Base (FAQ #5926), and in that case you can't legally play Repulse at all — the ability still resolves.

question:
If units have already damage on them from a spell, and also no showdown takes place to heal them. Then opponent plays elder, do the damaged units die immediatly from elder static ("any damage is enough to kill units") ?

answer:
Yes — the pre-existing damage matters, and those units die the moment Elder Dragon hits the board (provided that damage was dealt by Elder Dragon's controller).

Elder Dragon's static doesn't deal damage; it redefines lethal damage for units carrying damage marked by its controller, so any non-zero amount is lethal (CR 142.4.c, 323.4). Spell damage stays marked until the end of turn — it only heals after combat or during the end-of-turn cleanup — so it's still sitting there when the Dragon enters, and a cleanup runs before anyone gets priority to react to the "when you play me" trigger (FAQ 10686, FAQ 11876). No showdown or combat in between makes no difference; if anything, it just means nothing healed the damage away.

The one real condition: "your damage" is relative to the Dragon's controller. If the earlier spell was cast by the Dragon player's opponent, that damage is not theirs, and the passive won't make it lethal.

question: assume i have a zhonyas hidden, my opponent hollows breath's that battlefield and then plays elder. Do i have a window to play the zhonya's? If so, can my opponent target the saved unit with elder's ability afterwards
answer:
Yes, you get the window.

Facedown cards have Reaction, so you flip Zhonya's in reaction to Bellows Breath while it's on the chain. Zhonya's is a gear permanent, so it resolves immediately and its replacement effect is live before Bellow Breath resolves; when Bellow Breath would kill your unit, Zhonya's kills itself instead, and the unit is healed, exhausted, and recalled to Base (Rule 369). If it doesn't kill your unit, damage just stays marked.

Afterwards, yes — your opponent can absolutely target the saved unit with Elder Dragon. Elder's play effect chooses "up to one enemy unit at each location," and your Base is one of those locations, so the recalled unit is a legal choice there. Because Elder's passive makes any of its controller's damage lethal, the 1 damage kills it, and Zhonya's is already used up (it died as its own replacement cost). Nothing about the save grants protection.

If your unit would have survived the Bellows Breath and have the 1 damage still marked, it would die when Elder Dragon enters play. Since Elder Dragon entered play, it's 'when you play me' ability is added as pending to the chain and since Elder Dragon left the chain we run a cleanup. In this cleanup your unit dies due to Elder Dragons passive and still having 1 damage marked from the opponents Bellows Breath. If you played your Zhonya's in reaction to Bellows' breath, it saves your unit and recalls it healed to base. Now we finalize the Elder Dragon 'when you play me' ability. Your saved unit now in base can be chosen as a target at a location. Your base is a legal location.

If you however did not play it before that and all your units at battlefields are killed, you will still have a window when Elder Dragon's When you play me ability goes on the chain. It's not an optional triggered ability so it will go on the chain, its controller has to finalize it. Afterwards because the chain is still not empty at this point, you can play your zhonya's and potentially save a unit in another location or just save your gear from being trashed.

The location trick only works in the other order: if Elder's play effect has already locked in the unit at the battlefield and you recall it before that ability resolves, it stops fulfilling the targeting restriction and is unaffected (2026-04-29 Elder Dragon clarification). Once it's sitting at Base before Elder is played, it's fair game.

Note: I couldn't find a card named "Hollow Breath" in the database — if it's a spell that deals damage/kills at that battlefield, the ruling above holds as written.

question: My opponent let hextech ray finalize killing his unit. And is now saying that he wants to react with janna to save it. It is my turn, can she heal and save it? is there a chain open?

question: how burn out works
answer:
Burn Out is a forced replacement effect that happens when you try to move more cards out of your Main Deck than are actually in it (CR 432).

The sequence is: do as much of the action as possible, Recycle your Trash into your Main Deck (randomized), choose an opponent to gain 1 point, then finish the rest of the instruction. So if you're told to Draw 4 with 3 cards left, you draw 3, shuffle your trash back in, then draw the 4th — you don't burn out mid-draw (CR 414.4, FAQ #3374). Same for Burning/trashing cards: burn what you can, burn out, then burn the rest.

Only actions that actually move cards out of the deck cause it. Looking at or Revealing cards in excess of your deck size does not burn you out — the cards are still in the Main Deck zone while revealed (CR 432.1.c, FAQ #5695).

If your deck and Trash are both empty, you burn out repeatedly, one point to an opponent each time, and after the first Burn Out those points can't be replaced or prevented. Points gained this way can be the winning point — they aren't restricted like Conquer or Hold — and the win happens immediately if it pushes someone past the Victory Score with more points than everyone else (CR 432.3.c.1).

question: What happens to a player in FFA when they attempt to draw from an empty deck?
answer:
They Burn Out. They draw as many as possible (none), recycle their trash into their Main Deck (randomized), choose an opponent to gain 1 point, then finish the draw instruction (CR 432.2).

In FFA the only difference from 1v1 is that "choose an opponent" is a real choice among multiple opponents — you pick who gets the point. If the deck and trash are both empty, you'll Burn Out repeatedly, handing out 1 point each time until an opponent reaches the Victory Score (8 in FFA3/FFA4) and wins (CR 432.3).

Note that points from Burn Out aren't subject to the final-point restriction that applies to Conquer, so a Burn Out point can win the game at match point (FAQ 7293).

When combat resolves to "No Result" with units from both players still there, the game stages a fresh Showdown and Combat at that battlefield (CR 468.3.d.1), and the first combat formally ends at 466.7 — designations removed, "this combat" effects expiring. Your opponent is still the attacker (they applied Contested, CR 466.2.c.1), so when the new combat opens Vi gains the Attacker designation for the first time in that combat and stuns an enemy unit "here" — which can be the Deathknell unit.

Two caveats: she still only stuns one unit, not the whole battlefield (FAQ #10205), and she must be alive and still at that battlefield when the trigger resolves, since "here" is checked on execution (FAQ #10045). question: LeBlanc, Deceiver interaction with gusting. If I react to the initial trigger and gust all valid targets, what happens? If I react to the reflexive trigger and gust the chosen target, what happens?

Reacting to the reflexive trigger is the cleaner line: Gust resolves first (LIFO), sending the already-chosen copy target to hand — a non-board zone, which severs the targeting relationship — so the copy instruction mistargets and does nothing, per Rule 359.3.e.7. The token is already on the board as a 0 [M] unit and keeps its granted Temporary, so it dies at the start of its controller's next Beginning Phase, before scoring.

If you'd rather kill the token outright, Gust it instead in that second window — it's a legal target while still 0 [M], and a token sent to hand ceases to exist, leaving nothing to copy and no Temporary to matter.

question: how does diana lunari work? do you check and recycle optionally before reveal?

question: if i play two spells in reaction to themselves, so two on chain. the 2nd spell counts a played first since its resolved first for heron. but then the discount says my next card is discounted. does that mean the first card on the chain which has not resolved yet will be my 2nd card played? or the next play from hand? how does this discount work here?
answer:
No — the card still sitting on the chain doesn't get the discount. The discount only applies to the next card you newly play after the trigger resolves.

You're right that the reaction spell resolving first counts as your "first card played" (FAQ #11688), so Heron triggers when that one finishes resolving. But Heron discounts "the next card played (added to the chain and queued for finalization) this turn after the ability resolves" (FAQ #11762) — your first spell was added to the chain long before the trigger resolved, so it's exempt. It resolves at full price, no matter that it's still on the chain when the discount appears.

So the sequence is: spell B resolves → Heron triggers → trigger resolves, creating the discount → spell A resolves undiscounted → the very next card you play from hand this turn (or any Reaction you squeeze in right there, before A resolves) gets the [2][A][A] reduction. Note it's "this turn" only — if you don't play anything else before the turn ends, the discount expires.

question: With the new mistargeting rules: When I play Gust on a viable target at Abandoned Hall and the spell is reacted to, so that the unit goes to more than 3 Might. answer:
Yes — your unit still gets the +1. Abandoned Hall's trigger cares only that a spell was played, not that it had a legal target when it resolved. Gust mistargets (Rule 359.3.e.7 — the instruction doesn't execute), but per Rule 359.3.e.10 a spell with no effect "is still considered played," so the trigger condition is met.

Timing also works in your favor: the Abandoned Hall trigger is placed on the chain only after Gust finishes resolving (FAQ 11036/11415), so your unit is still sitting there and is a legal choice when the trigger resolves. You choose the unit as the trigger is finalized, so you can pick whichever unit you control at that battlefield.

One caveat — this only holds because Gust resolved. If it were countered instead, the spell is not considered played and Abandoned Hall would not trigger at all (FAQ 10646).

question: how do i play my chosen champ and does it go straight to bench or can i also put it in battlefield
answer:
You play your Chosen Champion exactly like any other unit: pay its cost from the Champion Zone, and choose the location it enters — your Base or any battlefield you already control. It's not locked to Base.

It enters exhausted (unless you pay Accelerate), and it can't go to a battlefield you're attacking/contesting, since a contested battlefield isn't one you control yet — units played during that combat go to Base instead (Rule 355.2.a, FAQ #3843). The Champion Zone is basically a revealed extension of your hand: no abilities usable from there, and you need the Reaction keyword to play it during a Closed State.

Because the chain resolves last-in-first-out, your Sprite Call resolves first and creates the new Sprite token, then the original Temporary trigger resolves and kills the old one. The new Sprite isn't checked for Temporary until your next Beginning Phase, so it stays.

question: how does the end turn phase work. when it goes to other player whats the rule , also how many cards do you draw at the very start of the game
answer:
The Ending Phase is the two-step wrap-up of your turn (Rule 317).

Ending Step — "at the end of the turn" effects fire here. Abilities like Annie's or Dazzling Aurora's triggers go on the Chain and resolve through normal FEPR, so opponents can respond with Reactions only because a Chain exists — not because the phase changed.

Expiration Step — an Ending Special Cleanup runs, inserting: all units heal all damage, all "this turn" effects expire simultaneously, and every player's Rune Pool empties (unspent Energy and Power are lost). If any items went through FEPR during this step (e.g. a trigger fired), you loop back to the start of the Expiration Step and do it again (317.2.f). Once clean, the next player in the turn queue becomes the Turn Player.

One quirk worth knowing: that heal is global — every unit in play heals, including ones at Base that never fought. Also, since the Expiration Step loops, damage dealt by a trigger resolving there doesn't carry into the next turn.

question: do you have to pay rune to equip items to your tokens?
answer:
Yes — tokens are units, so equipping to them works exactly as normal and you pay the full Equip cost.

Equip is an activated ability short for "[Cost]: Attach this gear to a unit you control" (Rule 818.1.c.2), and a token unit is a unit for all effects and actions that choose units (Rule 185.2.d; FAQ 9299 confirms attaching gear to a Sprite token). There is no free-equip rule for tokens: you pay whatever the Equip cost says — energy, power (recycling the rune for a domain symbol), or any non-resource cost listed (Rule 818.1.c.3).

The only discount path is a card-granted one, e.g. Emperor of the Sands gives your Sand Soldier tokens Weaponmaster, which reduces the Equip cost by [A] — still a payment, just smaller. Note that an already-attached gear can't be re-equipped without Weaponmaster, since its rules text goes inactive (Rule 718.2).

question: If opponent does action , and I do nothing in response I pass my action turn, can he do another action or does combat start
answer:
Combat does not start — he can play another action. Passing in response to his action doesn't end the showdown by itself.

Here's the flow: his Action resolves, then Focus passes to you (Rule 346). You get the next opportunity — play something or pass. If you pass, Focus goes back to him, and he's free to start another action chain. The showdown only closes (and combat proceeds to the damage step) when both players pass consecutively without either playing anything (Rule 348, FAQ #2268).

So the showdown keeps going as long as either of you keeps starting new chains — your single pass is not enough to force combat.

question: If a glasc mixologist dies in the beggining phase, can the unit generated by its deathknell hold that battlefield and therefore score to 8?
answer:
Yes — provided the death happens before your Beginning Phase's Scoring Step.

The Beginning Phase is a Beginning Step followed by a Scoring Step that Holds every battlefield you control (CR 315.2.b, 471.2). If Glasc Mixologist dies during that Beginning Step — say, to a start-of-phase trigger or a spell played in an Open state before the step resolves — its Deathknell goes on the chain as a Pending Item before it hits the trash, and because an item is on the chain you can't lose control of the battlefield in the meantime (same reasoning as FAQ #9149). You resolve the Deathknell, play the unit to that battlefield you control, and it's still there when the Scoring Step runs — so you Hold and gain the point.

That point can absolutely be the eighth: the Final Point restriction in CR 473.1.b applies only to points gained through Conquer, and points from other sources aren't beholden to it.

The timing caveat is real, though. If Glasc dies after your Scoring Step has already passed (Channel or Draw Phase), you get no point that turn — the Hold window is gone and you can't score that battlefield again this turn (CR 472).

question: If Diana Lunari is dealt lethal damage by a Shurkien Flip and an empowered Akali Deadly weapon moving into that battlefield, can I still trigger Diana Lunari's ability?
answer:
No — Diana's ability won't trigger, because she's dead before the Showdown actually begins.

Her trigger checks "when a showdown begins here," and by the time the Combat Showdown opens, she's no longer at that battlefield. Moving is instantaneous, and Akali's "When I move" trigger is placed on the chain and fully resolves before any showdown can start — a Combat/Showdown only begins in a Cleanup with an empty chain, and showdowns/combats are staged and opened at the very end of the cleanup (CR 323.7–323.12, 462). So Shuriken Flip's 2 damage resolves, then Akali's move trigger adds 2 more, and Diana (3 Might) dies during the cleanup at step 3b — which runs before Step 9/10 begins the Showdown/Combat (CR 323.4).

By the time the Showdown begins she has already left the battlefield, so the "when a showdown begins here" condition can't be evaluated for her (Rule 383.2.c.2). This is different from removal after the fact: if her trigger were already on the chain, it would resolve independently of her (FAQ #10222) — but here it never gets placed at all. Note also that the Akali trigger damage is what makes the damage lethal; either way it resolves pre-showdown, and if Diana were the only opposing unit, that battlefield becomes a Non-Combat Showdown.

question: I have a unit at 0 or even negative might. When this turn ends, will it be granted any status or keyword like "temporary" that will kill it next turn? Or is its might return to normal when the turn ends?
answer:

At the end of the turn the Expiration Step heals all units and expires every "this turn" effect simultaneously, so the Might modifiers fall off and the unit goes back to its printed/base Might plus any persistent modifiers (attached Gear bonuses, passive abilities) — Rule 317.2.

Also worth separating: 0-or-less Might is never itself lethal. The unit only dies if it has non-zero damage equal to or exceeding its Might (CR 143.2.b), so a 0-Might unit with no damage simply survives the turn.

The one case where it does die next turn is if it genuinely has Temporary (e.g., a Sprite token) — that trigger kills it at the start of its controller's Beginning Phase before scoring, independent of its Might.

question: In 2v2 mode (Magma Chamber), the opponent moves in to fight my ally at a battlefield they control. Can I play Rengar, Trophy Hunter as a reaction to help defend my ally?
answer:
No — Rengar can't be played to that battlefield to help your ally.

Combat can only ever occur between units controlled by exactly two players (CR 464), and a battlefield with a Staged Combat or Combat in Progress is an invalid destination for a unit controlled by anyone who isn't already a participant — by any means, including Ambush (CR 464.2). Once the opponent's unit moves in against your teammate's unit, those two players are the combatants; you're a third player, so Rengar has no legal landing spot there. Rengar's expanded Ambush permission ("even if you don't have units there") only widens which battlefields are normally valid — it doesn't override the multi-player combat restriction, and if an effect forced a unit there anyway it would be played to your Base instead (CR 464.2.a).

Note that a "friendly/teammate" designation doesn't change this — combat still counts distinct players, and your teammate's Defenders don't become yours. You can still play the Rengar itself during the turn (just to your Base or a battlefield you legally control), and you're free to help your ally with Reaction spells/abilities, since teammates can be invited to play cards with priority (CR 491.8.a).

question: if you play ruined rex. then target it with baited hook. it dies and you choose a target for its deathknell before you draw for baited hook correct? and in which case its on the chain. if your baited hook gives you karthus is that ruined rex 4 damage now doubled? does it double the chain item or double the amount of times it goes on chain?

Close, but two corrections — and the short answer is no, you don't get doubled damage.

You don't choose the Deathknell target before the draw. When Ruined Rex dies, its Deathknell trigger is created and added to the chain as a pending item right away (Rule 808.1.d.2), but it can't finalize — and targets are only chosen at finalization — until Baited Hook has fully finished resolving. So the target is picked after you look at the top 5 and play Karthus, and Karthus will already have entered before the trigger is placed on the chain.

Despite that, Karthus does not double it. His ability reads "Your [Deathknell] effects trigger an additional time," and it only applies if he's already on the battlefield at the moment the trigger is created. Here the trigger was created while Karthus was still in your deck, so you get one trigger and 4 damage, not 8.

On the last question: Karthus doubles the number of triggers (a second, separate chain item, resolved one at a time), not the damage value — so Ruined Rex would deal 4 twice, never 8 in one hit. This matches the established Baited Hook/Karthus line (FAQ #11068, #10051).

question: Does baited hook kill friendly unit part of finalization or resolution
answer:
Resolution. Baited Hook's kill is part of the ability's effect, so it happens when the ability resolves — not during finalization.

Its cost is only [1][C] plus exhausting [E]; "Kill a friendly unit" sits in the effect text and executes top-to-bottom at resolution (Rule 158.1). What happens at finalization is only the choose/target step — you pick which friendly unit to kill when the ability is placed on the chain, which is why opponents get a Reaction window before the kill actually occurs.

Practically: if the chosen unit is removed or bounced in response, nothing gets killed, the "killed unit" reference is null, and you look at 5 cards but can't play any of them. The kill instruction does create the pending Deathknell trigger before the unit hits the trash (CR 429.1.a.1.b), and per LIFO that trigger resolves after the rest of Baited Hook finishes.

answer:
Yes — Startipped Peak can only trigger once per turn for each player, though that's because of the scoring limit, not card wording.

question: how can you allocate dmg. can i spread out 7 dmg to 7 diff units even if none will die
answer:
No — you can't spread damage freely. Combat damage is assigned one unit at a time, and each unit must receive lethal damage in full (non-zero damage equal to or exceeding its Might) before you assign any damage to the next unit (CR 467.2.c.3).

So with 7 damage you'd kill at most two units (3 + 3, with 1 left over to a third) if the units have 3 Might, not sprinkle 1 on seven units. You also can't over-assign: a unit can't receive more than the minimum lethal amount unless no further units remain to receive damage (CR 467.2.c.4) — that's the only case where the leftover lands all on one unit.

Two exceptions worth knowing: a unit that can't be dealt damage at all (e.g., damage fully prevented or "I don't take damage") is exempt from the mandatory-assignment math (465.2.c.10), and effects that redefine lethal — like Elder Dragon's "any amount of your damage is enough to kill enemy units" — let you assign just 1 to each unit and move on. Tank/Backline shift who gets assigned damage first, but never let you skip the lethal-in-full requirement.

question: I'm using the icathian rain , and the opponent has 1 Predator on their base In this way, can I stop after giving only 2 damage to the deflect unit? Is it possible to pause the gameplay midway because the deflection feels overwhelming when making a judgment?
answer:
Short answer: Deflect never caps how much damage you deal — it's a cost, so "stopping at 2" depends entirely on what's dealing the damage, not on the Deflect unit.

If you're dealing a fixed amount to a chosen target (a spell like Falling Star or a 2-damage effect), you deal exactly what the card says; you can't reduce it to 2. Deflect just adds mandatory Power when you choose that permanent (Rule 809.1.c), and it's paid even if the damage ends up prevented or the ability later fizzles (FAQ #2811). If you have no other targets you will have to deal all the instances to the predator with deflect as you need to be able to execute the spell fully. However, you can not play the spell and this will prevent you from paying the extra deflect, even "mid cast". On finalization you realize you don't want to play this, you absolutely can as long as it has not become completely finalized. You will have revealed a card, but you won't lose your runes in the process.

Where "stopping at 2" does work is with Repeat: you can simply decline to pay the Repeat cost and let the spell execute only once, so the Deflect unit takes just the base 2 damage — but the Deflect cost is mandatory per time you choose it, so if you do pay to repeat and target that unit again, you owe Deflect a second time (FAQ #9293).

question: When you play multiple units with one card, do they count as two separate times you play a unit or one?
answer:
Two — each unit is played individually, so playing two units off one card is two separate "play a unit" events, even though the card itself is only one card played.

When an effect tells you to play units, each one goes through the full Play process on its own (CR 420.3.b — treat all steps of Play as normal). So "when you play a unit" triggers fire once per unit: Vanguard Captain's two Recruit tokens each count as a unit played (they're played, not just created — Rules 350.2, 182.1.a), triggering such effects twice.

Two caveats: the card still counts as only one card played (so Legion/"second card" style checks see one card, not two), and a trigger worded "the first time you play a unit each turn" still fires only once even if both units are played simultaneously, since the controller picks one instance (Rule 383.1.b).

question: When Orianna transforms a gear into a unit, do abilities printed in the gear's rules-text box trigger and resolve when that gear-unit conquers or holds. For example when she makes Warmog equipment a unit, will its conquer effect trigger?
answer:
No — as written, the conquer/hold abilities on Equipment sit in the effect text box (below the Equip line), and effect text is Inactive unless the card is Attached (Rule 724). Orianna's Lady of Clockwork makes the gear a unit gear, which grants it unit properties but does not Attach it, so "When I conquer, buff me" on Warmog's Armor would not trigger or resolve.

The distinction is where the text is printed. The Equip line is Rules Text and stays active (Rules Text is never inactive by default, Rule 723), so the thing can still be equipped later — but the triggered ability in the lower box does not fire while the card is unattached, and Inactive abilities "do not trigger, do not apply" (Rule 721.2). Being a unit doesn't change that; it just means it won't be recalled off the battlefield (Rule 178.1.a.1.a).

Note the flip side: if the equipment is attached when it matters, its effect text becomes active and is appended to the unit it's attached to (Rule 136.2.c) — in that case the host unit is the one that has the conquer/hold trigger, not the gear itself. No FAQ covers Lady of Clockwork specifically; this reads off the Inactive text rules.

Long Sword's Might Bonus (+2, Rule 137.3) makes Mournful Witness a 4-Might unit, so she survives Akali's first move-in trigger (2 damage) and the Combat Showdown actually opens with her as the Defender. When B activates Rogue Assassin during that Showdown, Akali's move-out trigger fires for another 2 — that's 4 damage on a 4-Might unit, which is lethal.

Lethal units are Killed in the cleanup that follows (CR 323.4), and that cleanup runs while the Showdown/Combat is still ongoing — before the Showdown closes and the combat's resolution step. Combat doesn't end until Step 466.7 (after Combat Cleanup, combat result, and Establish Control), so the damage is dealt first, during the combat, and combat ends afterward. Had she survived to combat end, she'd have been healed by Combat Cleanup and then empowered — but she's already in the trash by then, so no empower.

question: Does my opponent's defending unit immediately stop being a defender if my only attacking unit leaves combat?
answer:
No — the defending unit keeps its Defender designation. Designations are only removed when Combat fully ends (CR 468.7.a), or if that unit itself leaves the battlefield the combat is taking place at (Rule 323.2.c).

An attacker leaving, dying, or being recalled doesn't end the combat either — it stays active until all players pass Focus consecutively, and cards that care about "while it's a defender" keep applying. Same logic runs the other way: an attacker keeps its Attacker designation even if the defender moves away or the combat becomes unopposed (FAQ 1398, 4660).

The only exception is if the defending unit itself is moved off that battlefield (or its controller changes) — then a Cleanup strips the designation from it, which can matter for abilities like Assault/Shield that depend on it (FAQ 187).

question: How would svellsonger work with Riven
answer:
Yes — Svellsongur copies Riven, Shattered's printed text, so she gets a second instance of "When I attack, choose an enemy unit here. Deal 2 to it for each Equipment attached to me."

The copied ability is appended to Riven's rules text, so both instances trigger on the same attack and go on the Chain as separate triggers, resolving one at a time. Each instance deals 2 per Equipment attached to her, and Svellsongur itself counts as attached Equipment — so with just Svellsongur on her, that's 4 total damage (2 + 2), split between two independently chosen enemy units at her battlefield if you want. Two Svellsongurs would give three instances (they only copy printed text, so copies don't compound — FAQ #1141).

One thing that doesn't work: the copied Weaponmaster does nothing. question: How would svellsonger work if Riven already has gear on her
answer:
Short answer: it works fine — Svellsongur copies only Riven's printed text, so the gear already on her isn't copied, but she does end up with a second copy of her own abilities.

Riven's "when I attack, deal 2 to an enemy unit here for each Equipment attached to me" gets duplicated by Svellsongur, so both instances trigger on attack and each one counts all Equipment attached to her (Svellsongur included). With one other Equipment on her, that's 4 damage per trigger, 8 total, split across whatever targets you choose for each trigger. Whatever the pre-existing gear grants her doesn't feed into the copy — copies take the object's original traits regardless of later alterations, and attachment order doesn't matter (FAQ #8410; Effect Text only becomes active while Attached, Rule 724). Stacking more Svellsongurs gives one extra instance each, not doubled instances — three Svellsongurs on Riven means four total instances of her text, not eight.

One caveat: this only matters for her text. Attached Equipment still gives its normal Might bonus on top; Svellsongur has no Might bonus of its own and doesn't amplify it.

question: When both players pass priority in succession, what happens to the pending chain?
answer:
The newest item on the chain resolves — and only that one item.

When both players pass in sequence without adding anything, you move to Step 4: Resolve, and the newest Finalized Chain Item resolves in full (Rules 339.1, 340.1). The chain is LIFO, so this is the top item, not the whole chain.

After that single resolution, all players get priority again and can respond before the next item resolves (FAQ #7640, Rule 340.4). If nothing is added and everyone passes again, the next item resolves — repeat until the chain is empty, at which point play returns to an Open State and (in a Showdown) Focus passes to the next player in turn order.

question: What if I pass focus and my opponent passes focus in showdown
answer:
It closes the Showdown — when all players pass Focus in sequence without playing anything, the Showdown ends (Rule 348, see also 347.2.a).

What happens next depends on the type. If it was a Combat Showdown, you proceed to the Combat Damage Step and then Combat Cleanup (which heals all units in play). If it was a Non-Combat Showdown, no damage step and no healing: if only one player's units remain at the battlefield, that player Establishes Control and Conquers if they haven't already scored it this turn (Rule 348.2).

One nuance: the pass that matters is passing Focus while the chain is empty, and it takes all players passing in sequence. A pass after a chain resolves is just Focus auto-moving to the next player in turn order — that's not the same as a player passing, so the Showdown doesn't end there (see FAQ 1797).

question: If I have 4 gears on the field attached to 4 units, when I cast "Arise!", how many sand soldier tokens can I get?
answer:
4 tokens — as long as all four of those gears are actually Equipment.

Arise! reads "Play a 2 [M] Sand Soldier unit token for each Equipment you control," and Equipment means Gear with the Equipment tag (Rule 150). Plain Gear like a Gold token or a non-Equipment relic doesn't count, so if even one of your four isn't Equipment you'd only get 3.

Attachment is irrelevant to the count — attached Equipment is still Equipment, still Gear, and still controlled by you (FAQ #2018), and nothing limits how many can be attached. The only real snag is the back half: "Then do this: Ready up to two of them" creates a pretty complex chain. Example with 3 equipment on the board:

Play Arise - both players pass priority- Arise resolves
3 Sand Soldier token units added as pending to the chain, end part reflexive trigger of Arise added as pending

Order of pending chain items: SS 1, SS 2, SS 3, reflexive trigger

SS 1 finalizes and enters at a location, it's weaponmaster is added as a pending item at the back of the existing chain

order of pending chain items: SS 2, SS 3, reflexive trigger, SS 1 weaponmaster

Repeat this process for SS 2 & 3: three SS token units on the board and pending chain item order is reflexive trigger > SS 1 weaponmaster > SS 2 weaponmaster > SS 3 weaponmaster

The rflexive trigger finalises first and requires a target (0/1/2 units that were previously created), it lingers on chain, SS 1 WM finalises (target an equipment and lingers on the chain), SS 2 WM, SS 3 WM

So the chain of finalized items is now reflexive trigger at bottom, SS 1 WM, SS 2 WM, SS 3 WM, this resolves Last In First Out (LIFO) as normal.

This means your opponent will know all units locations, what equipment each will get and which will become ready before they can respond when they receive priority.

The only way the hidden card dies here is if you send the unit somewhere else and that battlefield was your only presence there — then after the chain clears, the next cleanup removes hidden cards from battlefields you don't control and trashes them (CR 323.6.a).

question: If you Heedless Resurrection on a Elnuk played from hidden, how does it resolve? does the Elnuk recycle itself from the trash and do you get the +3?

When the Elnuk's trigger resolves, the card is in your trash, so the ability can't reference the unit to determine which battlefield it was hidden at — its instructions are ignored. question: What rules pertain to disruptive spectators and players around play area?
answer:
Disruptive behavior at or around the play area is covered by the Tournament Rules, mainly spectator role rules (204.8) and Unsporting Conduct (704) — note that a player who is at the event but not currently in a match counts as a spectator (204.8.b), so those rules follow them too.

Spectators must remain silent during matches, may not personally point out rules or policy violations to players, and may not give strategic advice (204.8.c.1, 204.8.d.1–2). At Professional OPL they also can't ask players to pause play while they flag a judge — they can only alert a judge directly. Players can request that a judge remove a spectator from their match, and competition officials can order a spectator not to observe a match at any time (204.8.e–f).

For players, 204.7 requires respectful behavior toward all attendees, including spectators. Unsporting Minor is a Warning (disrespect, bullying, offensive materials); Unsporting Major is a Disqualification and often means ejection from the venue (704.2–704.3), and the head judge can apply any penalty up to DQ for conduct issues since the listed infractions aren't exhaustive (704.1.c). Deliberately distracting an opponent so they miss a priority window is Angle Shooting, and judges may intervene in a match when they observe unsporting conduct (704.4.a.6, 701.1.d.3).

Two adjacent ones worth knowing: giving a player advice from outside the match is Outside Assistance (the recipient gets a Match Loss unless they refuse it by calling a judge, and an advising spectator can be barred from the venue — 703.9), and players must keep their cards above the level of the playing surface while a spectator is around (424.1).

question: If a combat showdown begins with me having an assault unit at the battlefield and my opponent having 1 other unit at the same battlefield and their unit is removed during the showdown, does my unit retain assault even though it is alone at the battlefield? Does the showdown stay a combat showdown?
answer:
Yes to both — Assault is tied to the Attacker designation, not to whether an opposing unit is still sitting across from it.

Assault is "While I am an attacker, I have +X [M]," and it stays in effect as long as the unit keeps the Attacker designation (Rule 807.1.d.1). Attacker/Defender designations are only removed at the end of Combat (CR 468.7.a) or from a unit that itself leaves the battlefield — an enemy unit dying or being bounced doesn't strip your unit's designation, so your Assault bonus persists until Combat ends. FAQ #1195 is directly on point: Assault applies in combat showdowns until the end of combat, even if the defender moves its units out.

Likewise the showdown remains a Combat Showdown once it has opened as one. Removing units mid-showdown doesn't end it or revert it to non-combat — it still closes only when both players pass consecutively, and it runs through the Resolution Step (FAQ #757, #776). Practically, since only your unit remains at the battlefield, the Combat Damage Step is skipped (CR 467.1 requires both Attacking and Defending units present) and you win the Combat in the Determine Combat Result task. Note the flip side: if your Assault unit is the one that leaves the battlefield, it loses the Attacker designation and Assault falls off immediately.

question: Glass mixologist trigger can target deathknell unit on your bf that died at same time and why?

Since an item is on the chain, you also can't lose control of the battlefield during the following cleanup — so the graveyard unit is a legal choice and the battlefield is a legal destination. Because of how you cannot finalize when a cleanup is happening, you will only finalize the chain item, once all units are in the trash. You control both triggers, so you choose their order (Rule 808.2.a): resolve Glasc Mixologist's first, play the just-died unit from your trash (as long as it meets Glasc's cost limit), and it enters at that same battlefield.

The why: Deathknell "remembers" state from before death, and the pending chain item freezes control of the battlefield until the trigger resolves (FAQ #9783, and the Unleashed clarification that control can't be lost while an item is pending). Caveat: if you're the attacker at an opponent's battlefield, you don't control it, so you can't play the unit there (FAQ #10612).

question: If I use Temporal Breach a gear turned into a unit by Orianna’s legend ability, does it get replayed as a gear, as a unit gear, or does it stay banished?
answer:
It comes back as a plain Gear, not a unit gear — and because it lands at a battlefield as an unattached non-Unit Gear, it's Recalled to your Base in the next cleanup.

The banishment works fine (a unit gear is a unit, so it's a legal target), but the card changes zones to a non-board zone, which makes it a new object and clears all applied layer alterations — including Orianna's type change (Rule 124). At that point it's just its printed Gear card, and the "until you choose another gear" effect is gone; Orianna would have to choose it again at the start of a later Main Phase. Note it is not stuck in banishment: Temporal Breach specifies the location, which is the "unless an effect specifies otherwise" carve-out for playing Gear somewhere other than Base (Rules 149.2, 152.2) — so the replay is legal, it just enters as Gear and gets recalled as a corrective action (CR 459.1).

Net effect: you get the card back as a Base Gear (ready), it isn't a unit, and no Contested/Showdown results from the replay. If it was breached while at your Base, it simply re-enters at Base with no recall step needed.

question:

First irridescent trigger enter the chain, I react with from stone, exhausting my unit, then irrisdescent Avian finishes granting the +3, draw and channel 1
answer:
Yes — you can respond to an ability once it's finalized on the chain, but only with a Reaction card/ability.

Two corrections to the setup, though. Iridescent Avian's ability is an activated ability, not a trigger: "[T]: Buff a unit. If it's already buffed, give it +2 might this turn instead." It doesn't give +3 might, draw a card, or channel a rune — if you're getting that text from somewhere, you may be thinking of a different card. Activated abilities use the chain and also create a Closed State, so opponents do get to respond to it (Rule 377.3) — that part of your plan works.

Also, exhausting one of your units in response doesn't stop the Avian ability. Its cost (exhausting the Avian) was already paid when it was activated, and choices/targets lock in at finalization, so the buff/+2 might still resolves even if the source or your board changes.

Note: if you meant, can you pay the additional cost from Life from Stone with the activated ability of Iridescent Avian, then the answer is no, you can't. Like mentioned above, Avian's ability is a cost, so in order to put in on the chain, you need to pay that cost. Similarly with Life from Stone, you need to exhaust a friendly unit as an additional cost. You can't use that same unit in that scenario to pay both costs, unless you have a way to ready it before you would play Life from Stone.

question:
if i target a deflect unit and repeat with bellows breath. how much deflect do i pay? once or twice?

if i target the same unit with both instances of falling star, do i pay deflect once or twice?
answer:
Twice, in both cases. Deflect is charged per time your spell chooses the unit, not once per spell.

Deflect reads "cost [Deflect Value] more to play as an additional cost for each time they choose me" (Rule 809.1.c). Repeat makes you make fresh choices for the second execution during finalization (Rule 820.2), so choosing the same Deflect unit again on the repeat is a second choose → second Deflect payment. Same for Falling Star: its two separate "Deal 3 to a unit" instructions each choose a target, so pointing both at the same Deflect unit costs you Deflect twice (that's the confirmed FAQ #5107 / #3183 answer).

So Bellows Breath with Repeat hitting one Deflect 1 unit = 1 Energy + 1 Mind (base), + 1 Energy + 1 Mind (Repeat), + 2 Power of any domain for Deflect. Falling Star on a Deflect 1 unit with both instances = 2 extra Power. If you can't pay a Deflect charge, you can't make that choice.

Heads up: a couple of older FAQ entries describe Deflect as a one-time "binary" cost per spell, which conflicts with the current rule text above — the per-choosing reading is the one that matches Rule 809.1.c and the majority of rulings.

question: When a unit you control moves into a battlefield controlled by an opponent and you ambush Nidalee, Cat Form, then your opponent returns both the only enemy unit and Nidalee to hand with Star-Crossed, and you then replay that same Nidalee to the battlefield, does the replayed Nidalee still draw a card from her win condition even though she didn't see an enemy unit when she entered?
answer:
Yes — the replayed Nidalee still draws.

Combat doesn't stop just because the defending side loses all its units; it runs on until players pass and the Resolution Step completes (FAQ #7863). So the combat is still the same one when you replay Nidalee, she's a unit present at that battlefield during it, and she gains the Attacker designation in the cleanup following her entry (CR 466.2.c.3.a).

At Determine Combat Result, your side is the only player with units remaining, so you win and every unit you control at the battlefield inherits that result (CR 468.3.a/c). Her ability only asks whether she "remains after combat" — it has no requirement that an enemy unit was there when she entered, so she triggers and draws 1. (The original Nidalee that was bounced doesn't draw, since she wasn't at the battlefield when the result was determined.)

The one thing that would change this: if the Combat Showdown had already closed and combat ended before you replayed her, she'd be entering after combat and wouldn't win anything.

question: Do i score from holding before aurora is acitvated and used?
answer:
Yes — Holding scores during the Scoring Step of your Beginning Phase (Rule 315.2.b), which is at the start of your turn, so it happens well before Aurora's end-of-turn trigger ever goes on the chain.

Dazzling Aurora's trigger is checked "at the end of your turn," so it resolves in the Ending Phase, long after you've already Held. Order on a normal turn is: Awaken → Beginning (Beginning Step, then Scoring Step where you Hold and score) → Channel → Draw → Main (where you play Aurora) → End (Aurora triggers).

This is also why Aurora can finish a game at match point: if you Held one battlefield at the start of the turn and the unit Aurora plays at end of turn conquers a different battlefield, both scores happened in the same turn, satisfying the Final Point requirement (CR 473.1.b.1; FAQ 1317).

Because finalization makes you choose the trash target before paying costs, the unit you're bringing back just has to already be in your trash — you can't kill the Temporary unit and then pick that same unit (FAQ #9523). You then kill the Temporary unit as the additional cost; when the Temporary trigger later resolves, its "kill this" has nothing left to act on and does nothing.

question: 레이븐블룸 학생 2마리와 감시하는 보초 1마리가 있을 때, 내가 주문으로 감시하는 보초를 처치하면 레이븐블룸 학생의 스킬과 감시하는 보초의 죽음의 종소리는 어떤 순서로 처리돼?
answer:
레이븐블룸 학생 트리거 2개가 먼저 해결되고, 그다음 감시하는 보초의 죽음의 종소리(1장 뽑기)가 해결돼요.

이유는 체인에 올라가는 시점이 다르기 때문이에요. 카드는 완전히 해결(resolve)되어야 "플레이한 것"으로 취급되므로, 레이븐블룸의 "주문을 플레이할 때" 트리거는 주문이 해결을 끝낸 뒤에야 체인에 올라가요(CR 420.4.a). 반면 죽음의 종소리는 주문 해결 중 처치 지시가 실행되는 순간, 보초가 무덤으로 가기 직전에 이미 Pending Item으로 체인에 올라가 있어요(CR 429.1.a.1.b, 808.1.d.2). 체인은 나중에 올라간 것부터 풀리므로(LIFO), 뒤에 올라간 레이븐블룸 트리거가 먼저, 먼저 올라간 죽음의 종소리가 나중에 풀려요(FAQ #8210).

두 레이븐블룸 트리거끼리는 동시 트리거라 순서를 직접 고를 수 있고(둘 다 +1 might라 결과는 동일), 죽음의 종소리와는 동시 트리거가 아니라서 그 순서를 임의로 고를 수는 없어요. 보초의 조종자가 누구든 이 순서는 바뀌지 않아요.

question: Can you kill anothet friendly unit that died by combat damage with mordekaiser
answer:
Yes — as long as the other unit is still on the board when Mordekaiser's replacement applies.

Mordekaiser, Twice Slain reads "Once each turn, if I would die, you may kill a friendly unit to heal me, exhaust me, and recall me instead." If he and another friendly unit both take lethal combat damage, those deaths are simultaneous, and a replacement effect is applied before the qualifying events actually occur (Rule 370.1.c). The kill you perform as the cost — and Mordekaiser's heal/exhaust/recall — are carried out before the other simultaneous deaths resolve (Rule 373.1.a). So you can pick the other dying unit, kill it, and still save Mordekaiser.

The limit is that you can only kill a permanent whose origin is the board (Rule 429.2.a). If the other friendly unit already died earlier (it's sitting in the trash, not dying in this same cleanup), it's no longer a legal choice, and you'd need a different live friendly unit to pay the cost.

This is my interpretation based on the replacement-effect timing rules (Rules 370.1.c and 373). No official FAQ exists for this specific interaction.

answer:

Per FAQ #11528, Gutter Palace's "exactly 4 cards in hand and 4 units at battlefields" clause is part of the trigger condition and is checked when the trigger is placed on the chain, not on resolution. Temporary is just a triggered ability (Rule 816) — it kills Gutter Palace when it resolves, which is after the win trigger is already finalized on the chain, and it doesn't change your hand size or unit count anyway. The win trigger then resolves and you win.

The only case where Temporary would matter is if the 4-cards/4-units condition were already false at the start of the phase — then Gutter Palace never triggers and you don't win regardless of Temporary.

question:
can I score with deploy without a unit there and only the gear that has been deployed?

I mean without any units
answer:
No — a Deploy gear alone can't score. Scoring is either Conquer (gaining Control of a battlefield) or Hold (maintaining Control in your Beginning Phase), and Control is established only by having Units at a battlefield (Rule 190.4, 190.4.a); a gear is not a Unit, so with no units there you neither gain nor maintain Control. Contested status likewise comes only from a Unit becoming present (Rule 190.3.a), so a Deploy gear entering doesn't even start the Showdown that could lead to Control.

question: Is the resource obtained from the battlefield Threshhold of the Gray persist throughout the whole turn? Also is this energy only to be used during the showdown?
answer:
Yes. It stays in your Rune Pool for the rest of the turn, and there's no restriction forcing you to spend it during the showdown.

Threshold of the Gray reads "When combat starts here, the attacker and defender each [Add] [1]." All abilities with the action "Add" simply add Energy/Power to the Rune Pool (Rule 168), and a Rune Pool empties at the start of each player's Main Phase and at the end of each player's turn (Rule 167). Since combat happens during the Main Phase, that 1 Energy is still there afterward and lasts until end of turn — for both the attacker and the defender.

Unlike something like Diana, Scorn of the Moon (which explicitly says "Spend this Energy only during showdowns"), this card has no such wording, so the Energy can be spent on anything you can pay for later in the turn. The only caveat is that if you don't use it, it's lost at end of turn.

question: Does Sneaky Deckhand enter ready if played to an open battlefield with The Exile's ability?
answer:

The Exile readies units played to battlefields you control, but an "open" battlefield is defined as unoccupied and uncontrolled (CR 170.11.c). Sneaky Deckhand's permission lets you play to a battlefield you don't control; playing there just applies Contested (CR 190.3.a.1) and stages a Non-Combat Showdown, so Control isn't established until that Showdown closes as a Conquer. Since The Exile's condition is checked as the unit is played/enters, it won't see you in control, and the default "units enter exhausted" (CR 359.2.c) applies.

If you instead play Sneaky Deckhand to a battlefield you already control (its ability is permissive, not required), The Exile would make it enter ready — that's the only way this works. question: When Astral Heron is played with Here to Help , does Astral Heron apply his ability to his own cost when played
answer:
No — Astral Heron can't discount its own cost.

Heron's ability ("the next card you play this turn costs [2][A][A] less") only affects a card played after the trigger resolves. If Heron is your first card played and enters at a battlefield, it does see itself and trigger (FAQ #12236), but the reduction goes to the next card you play, not to Heron.

With Here to Help it's doubly clear: the unit is finalized as part of Here to Help's resolution, and Heron's ability is only added to the chain afterward — Heron is already on the board by then, so its own cost (already paid) can't be touched. The [3] discount from Here to Help applies to Heron's cost; and Heron's trigger has never triggered, as the first card played in that scenario was Here to Help (assuming Here to Help was the first card, but even if it wasn't Heron won't trigger).

question: If the unit that I have chosen to copy with Shady Spectacles die, what happen to the unit that Shady Spectacles attached to?
answer:
Yes — nothing happens to it. The equipped unit stays a copy of the unit you chose; the chosen unit dying doesn't detach Shady Spectacles or end the copy.

The printed duration is "for as long as this is attached to it" — the "it" is the equipped unit, so the copy effect lasts only as long as the Spectacles stay attached to that unit. It ends when the Spectacles detach or the equipped unit leaves play (the equipped unit dying kills the attachment, FAQ #12669), not when the copied unit does. There's also no re-choosing: you pick the unit once, as the Spectacles are attached.

So the equipped unit keeps using the chosen unit's copyable (printed) traits — name, type, tags, cost, domain, rules text, printed Might — and keeps everything of its own: buffs, statuses like Temporary or empowered, and any other gear attached to it (Rules 446.2, 479.1.b.1, 479.4).

One caveat the rules don't state outright: if the unit you chose was itself only a copy of something else (another Spectacles, a Mirror Image token, etc.), the copy effect's target is now a card in a new zone and its layer alterations are gone (Rule 124.1), so the traits carried over would be that card's printed ones. That's my interpretation — no official FAQ covers a copy source leaving play.

That's a triggered ability that goes on the chain, and because it makes the holder select a specific unit to move, that selection counts as choosing it (FAQ 8771). So if your opponent holds Amateur Recital and chooses your unit, it's an enemy ability that chooses a friendly unit — exactly what Not So Fast's Reaction window is for (FAQ 11189).

Nuances: it must choose a unit friendly to you. If the holder moves their own unit, or the ability targets nothing of yours, Not So Fast has no legal target and can't be played. question:
Hey judge, If I have Ahri, Confident on the battlefield and my opponent attacks with a 1 Might unit, will Ahri, Confident still trigger and gain +1 Might, even though my legend (Ahri, Nine-Tailed Fox) says "give it -1 Might, to a minimum of 1 Might"?

Radiance rules aren't published yet. This uses the printed card and current rules only, and it isn't a ruling on the new mechanics.

No — against a 1 Might attacker, Ahri, Confident does not trigger, because no Might is actually reduced. Ahri, Nine-Tailed Fox's -1 "to a minimum of 1" on a 1 Might unit is snapshotted as -0 (rule 479.4.b), so the unit's Might never comes down by 1 or more. Ahri, Confident's second ability reads "When you reduce the Might of an enemy unit here by 1 or more, give me +1 [M] this turn" — with an applied reduction of 0, that condition isn't met, so she gains nothing.

The distinction that matters: it's the applied reduction the ability checks, not the nominal "-1" on the legend. If the attacker has 2 or more Might, the legend reduces it by a real 1 or more, Ahri, Confident triggers, and she gains +1 Might this turn. Note the damage-style "treated as 0" clause on negative Might doesn't help here — that's for combat/damage math, and snapshotting means the reduction is tracked at 0.

This is my interpretation based on rule 479.4.b (snapshotting) and the printed card text. No official FAQ exists for this specific interaction.

question: My opponent is attacking into my battlefield with Vi, peacekeeper. If I reveal temporal breach and use it on my own unit, am I the attacker now?
answer:
No — you're still the defender, and your opponent is still the attacker. Attacker/Defender is fixed by who applied Contested to that battlefield, and that was your opponent when they moved into your battlefield with Vi, Peacekeeper (CR 466.2.c). Temporal Breach banishes your unit and replays it to the same location — a battlefield you already control — so your own unit re-entering applies no Contested, and the designation doesn't flip. Your replayed unit just rejoins as a Defender.

This is the same principle as the Rengar/Temporal Breach interaction (FAQ #11731): replaying units during combat doesn't reassign attacker/defender, and only a unit that first applies Contested makes its controller the attacker. Vi's own "when I attack" trigger already fired when she gained the Attacker designation at combat start, so nothing about your Temporal Breach changes her status either.

One note: since it's played from facedown, Temporal Breach must target a unit at the battlefield where it was hidden, so it has to hit a unit there (yours qualifies).

question: Can I assign all 5 damage to a unit at a battlefield using scorched earth when there is only 1 unit at that battlefield
answer:
Yes — with Scorched Earth you can put all 5 damage on a single unit, including when that unit is the only one at the battlefield. "Split" just sets the ceiling on how many targets you may divide it among; you can choose fewer than 5 units (Rule 355.14.c), and with only one unit there it's the only legal target anyway.

The combat restriction against over-assigning damage (Rule 467.2.c.4) doesn't apply here — that governs combat damage assignment, not spell damage. So the unit takes all 5, even if its Might is lower than 5.

question:
My enemy has a 5 might unit on a battlefield and combat starts, I attack and my enemy makes my unit move back with a spell. Is this a combat win for them?
Similarly, they star cross it, is this a combat win?
Similarly again, I get stunned, I cannot conquer and recall, this is a tie, correct?
answer:
Partly — they win the combat if only your unit leaves, but not if Star-Crossed clears the battlefield entirely; and a stun only makes it a tie if your unit survives the 5 damage.

Moved/returned to hand: Yes, that's a combat win for them. Once your attacker is gone, the Combat Damage step simply doesn't happen (no opposing units), but the combat still resolves in the Resolution Step, and 468.3.a gives the win to the player who is the only one with units there — the defender. So "when you win a combat" abilities trigger. They don't score a Conquer point though, since they already controlled that battlefield.

Star-Crossed: No. Star-Crossed returns a friendly unit and an enemy unit to hand, so their 5-might unit leaves too. With no units at the battlefield, the result is "No Result" (468.3.d — neither player has units present), so nobody wins the combat, and the battlefield actually becomes Uncontrolled (468.5.b). No conquer point, and no combat-win trigger.

Stunned attacker: It depends on your unit's might. The stun means it deals 0 damage while the defender assigns 5 to it — if your unit has 5 or less might it dies in the damage step, leaving them as the only player with units, so they win the combat. If your unit has 6+ might it survives, gets healed and then recalled during Combat Cleanup, and that recall forces "No Result" — a tie, no combat win for either side, and they keep the battlefield.

question: I move unit A to battlefield A and conquered it. Then I use Cataclysm to move my Jarvan IV, Royal Heir from base to battlefield B. Battlefield B has Riven, Broken Blade defending it. The opponent uses Siren's Song to move my unit at battlefield A to battlefield B as a reaction to my Cataclysm. Will a new combat showdown starts before or after Cataclysm resolves?
answer:
No new showdown starts before Cataclysm resolves — the Combat Showdown opens after it, once the Chain is empty.

Siren's Song is legal as a Reaction (Cataclysm's "opponents can't play spells this turn" only applies once Cataclysm has resolved), and it resolves first, moving your unit from battlefield A to battlefield B where Riven is defending. That applies Contested and gets a Combat staged, but the Chain still holds Cataclysm, so the turn isn't in a Neutral Open state (Rule 310.2) and the showdown just sits staged (Rule 323.11).

Then Cataclysm resolves, moving Jarvan IV into battlefield B. In the cleanup that follows resolution the Chain is empty, so the turn player initiates the staged showdown — and because units controlled by both players are present, it opens directly as a Combat Showdown/Combat (Rule 466.1).

One consequence worth noting: you are the Attacker, because the first unit to apply Contested to battlefield B was your unit A (moved by your opponent's own Siren's Song), so Jarvan IV enters the combat with the Attacker designation and Assault's +1 [M].

I have a hidden Evelynn, Entrancing at my battlefield with only a readied Stellacorn Herder equiped with Boots of Swiftness.

So the order is: Stellacorn's move is instantaneous, the draw trigger goes on the chain, the state closes, and you have a window to play Evelynn from facedown with Reaction (811.6) to the battlefield she was hidden at (811.1.d.1).

Playing her there also means you keep a unit at that battlefield, so you never lose control and never trigger the cleanup that trashes hidden cards for a battlefield you don't control (323.6.a). Afterwards her play effect resolves — since it requires "a different location," her target isn't restricted to that battlefield, so you can pull an enemy unit over from the other battlefield (811.1.d.3).

One caveat: Evelynn only gains Reaction the turn after she was hidden. If you hid her this same turn, you have no Reaction, and she'd be trashed when the trigger resolves and cleanup removes her for lack of control.

Your trigger then resolves, Vex sits at 1 Might with 1 damage marked, and it's killed in the following cleanup — a reduced-Might unit dies to damage already on it.

Even if the ordering were reversed, the result is the same: once Vex's trigger is on the chain it resolves independently of Vex's death, and the Stun and "can't move it this turn" effects persist for the rest of the turn (FAQ 12412). question: I have Clocktower Guardian defend a bf, he dies and I play a Unit for free now. Can I play him to the bf since the deathknell trigger is before conquer?
answer:
Yes — you can play the banished card to the battlefield Clocktower Guardian died at.

The Deathknell is put on the chain during the kill (Rule 383.2.c.3), so you still control that battlefield when it resolves: control can't change while a Combat is ongoing (190.4.b), and a cleanup can't take a battlefield from you while there's a pending chain item (190.4.c / 323.5). The Deathknell then resolves during the Combat Cleanup, which is before Determine Combat Result and the Establish Control/Conquer step (Rule 468), so that battlefield is still a legal location for you to play to. This is the same defender case as FAQ #2086 — it's the attacker in that position who can't play to the battlefield they're attacking.

Two corrections worth noting: the ability only ignores the card's Energy cost, so you still pay any Power it has. And the unit you play arrives during the cleanup, so it doesn't deal damage this combat — it's just present when the result is checked, which means both players have units there and the combat comes back as No Result, re-staging a Showdown and Combat rather than letting the attacker conquer on that pass.

question: when an opponent Graves (Blasting through) move from its base to battlefield, and I react with star crossed to send it to its owner hand. Is Its ability that deal damge to all units still activated?

Once he's back in hand he has a null Might and no location, so those instructions are Ignored (CR 359.3.f.2; FAQ #4917). No damage is marked, so nothing dies.

Two caveats. question: When bomb was triggered before or after ppoint?
answer:
Yes — the point is scored first; the Bomb's trigger goes on the chain afterward, so you can never kill the Bomb in time to stop the hold point.

Holding scores automatically with no priority window (FAQ #10523), and hold-based triggered abilities are only put on the chain as pending items after that point is gained (Rule 383.4.d.2.b). So the sequence is: opponent banks the hold point → Bomb's Deploy ("when an opponent holds here, kill this") goes on the chain and resolves → Bomb dies → its death trigger deals 2 to an enemy unit there. Note the Bomb only fires for the opponent of the Bomb's controller holding there, and that kill can't take the point back or let them re-score the same battlefield that turn (Rule 472).

question: How does last carress interact with Elnuk Herd
answer:
Yes — Last Caress lets you play Elnuk Herd from face down to any battlefield, but its +3 [M] play effect must then target a friendly unit at the battlefield you actually played it to, and Elnuk still recycles itself because it was played from face down.

Last Caress overrides the normal "a hidden permanent must be played to the battlefield it was hidden at" restriction (811.1.d.1), so you can drop Elnuk on a different battlefield. The targeting restriction is a separate rule and does not go away: for a permanent played from face down, the play effect's targets must come from options at the battlefield it was played to (811.1.d.3 — that rule's own example is literally a "next unit you play can be played to any battlefield" spell). So if you move Elnuk elsewhere, the +3 [M] is locked to that new battlefield, not where it was hidden. Elnuk itself counts, so you'll always have at least one legal target.

Then "recycle me if I was played from face down" still fires — Elnuk goes to the bottom of your Main Deck after handing out the +3 [M]. The Buff counter Last Caress gave it is wiped when it leaves play (705), so that part is effectively wasted on the Elnuk; the real value is the +3 [M] on another friendly unit and the surprise placement.

question: Stellwart goathert can destroy bomb
answer:
Yes — Stalwart Goatherd's play trigger can kill a Bomb gear token, including an opponent's, because it says "kill a gear" with no friendly restriction.

Bombs are tokens, and tokens have no cost — but their cost is treated as 0 for all purposes (Rule 185.3.a.1, with 206), so a Bomb comfortably satisfies "Energy cost [4] or less." The Bomb lives at a battlefield and Goatherd arrives at your base, but the trigger has no location restriction, so that doesn't matter. The trigger is a "may," so you can decline.

One thing to watch: killing a Bomb fires its Deathknell — deal 2 to an enemy unit there and kill all other Bombs its controller has there. "There" is the Bomb's battlefield, so if you have a unit at that battlefield, that 2 damage lands and can kill it; and each other Bomb killed that way triggers its own Deathknell in turn.

question: End turn step
answer:
No — the "end turn step" is not a window you can act in: when the turn player says they're ending their turn, nothing opens a priority window, so you can't play a reaction or activate anything at end of turn (FAQ 6113, 8978).

The Ending Phase is the Ending Step (at end of turn triggers and effects happen) followed by the Expiration Step, which heals all units, expires all "this turn" effects simultaneously, and empties both rune pools (Rule 317.2). Those steps resolve as Tasks with no discretionary actions granted to either player.

The only way to get to act there is if something is actually put on the Chain — a triggered ability firing "at the end of turn," or a legend/card that triggers in that phase — which gives you a Closed State to respond in with Reaction-timed cards. And note you can't squeeze in a Main-Phase-style action right before the turn ends either; off-turn priority only comes from a chain or a showdown.

question: Falling star target twice to a unit with deflect. How many deflect affected to me?
answer:
Yes — you pay the Deflect cost twice if both "Deal 3 to a unit" instances choose the same Deflect unit. Falling Star makes two separate choices, and Deflect charges "as an additional cost for each time they choose me" (Rule 809.1.c), so pointing both instances at that unit means paying its Deflect Value twice.

So a Deflect 1 unit costs an extra 2 Power total (any domain), a Deflect 2 unit 4 Power extra, on top of Falling Star's 2 Energy + 2 Power. If you can't pay a given Deflect charge, you can't make that choice — you'd have to send the second instance somewhere else.

Bellows Breath with Repeat should also charge Deflect twice if both times a unit with deflect is chosen.

Falling Star has two separate "Deal 3 to a unit" instructions inside a single execution, so it chooses twice with no Repeat at all — that's 2 cost increases on one card with Deflect, and 4 if you also repeat it. question: Does graves blasting through still deal damage as an attacker moving in if my opponent responds to the ability with sirens Siren's Song
answer:
No — if your opponent uses Siren's Song to move Graves off the battlefield before his attack trigger resolves, Graves deals no damage to the units there.

That's because "here" in "deal damage equal to my Might to all enemy units here" is a referent checked at resolution, not at trigger (Rule 359.3.f.2 — same principle as Yasuo, Remorseful being moved in response to his attack trigger, where "here" no longer matches). Once Siren's Song moves Graves, "here" is wherever he landed (normally his Base), so the ability hits whatever enemy units are at his new location — almost always nothing. His Might is likewise read at resolution, so any Might change would also be counted then.

Two caveats worth checking. Siren's Song needs a unit that moved this turn, which a Standard Move into the contested battlefield satisfies, but a unit merely played from hand has not moved (Rule 448.2) — so if Graves entered some other way, the spell can't legally target him. And the trigger still resolves and is still "played" even with nothing to damage; it just does nothing.

question: Do bomb token gears count as cards played
answer:
No — a Bomb token is a token, not a card, so playing one doesn't count as "playing a card." Rule 185 makes tokens their own object category ("Tokens are not cards"), and Rule 350.2 spells out that they can still be Played — that's playing a token, not playing a card. Legion and similar "if you have played another card this turn" checks specifically require a card, so Gold/Bomb-style token gears don't satisfy them (FAQ #4724, #9260).

What it does count as is playing a gear, because tokens keep their card type (FAQ #8803) — so triggers that ask for "when you play a gear" see it. (Compare FAQ #9440: playing a token unit is playing a unit.)

One thing worth separating out: Deploy is what lets the Bomb be played to a battlefield rather than your Base (Rule 830.1.b), and that's a permission change, not a change to what kind of object it is.

question: A player starts a chain and play an action. Is that same player can play a reaction before the others ?
answer:
Yes — you keep priority after playing your Action, so you can play a Reaction onto that same chain before opponents get a chance to respond.

Finalizing a card doesn't pass priority, and the controller of the newest chain item receives priority, so the first player with priority is the one who started the chain and may add another item to it (Rule 338.1.a.5). That only holds for another Reaction — you can't add a second Action to the same chain (only Actions can start a chain; once one exists, only Reactions can be added, Rule 309.1.a). Priority passes only when you choose to pass it.

question: Is it doable for a player that play a reaction to add another reaction before the opponent ? Or by extension as much as reaction as he wants before the other ?
answer:
Yes — the player who plays a Reaction keeps priority and can play another Reaction (and another) before ever passing to the opponent. Priority only moves when you explicitly pass it (Rules 311–312, 338.1.b), so there's no automatic hand-off after one Reaction. You're limited only by what you can afford, since costs are paid as each card goes on the chain.

If you do pass and your opponent also passes, the newest item on the chain resolves — and you don't get another window to react to that same item. After it resolves, priority opens up again and you can still respond to whatever is left underneath. Note the flip side: if your opponent passes back to you while a chain is open, you can also just keep adding Reactions rather than letting things resolve — Actions are the ones that require an empty chain.

question: Does Hunker Down stop the effects of siren Siren's Song, or any opponents "move a unit" effect
answer:
Yes — a unit under Hunker Down can't be moved by Siren's Song or any other opponent's move effect. Hunker Down's "It can't move this turn" is an absolute restriction, and move instructions that can't be followed are negated when the spell resolves, not merely delayed (Rule 54 "Can't beats Can"; Rule 359.3.e.14.b uses the same reasoning with Vilemaw's Lair's "units can't move from here to base").

The opponent can still cast Siren's Song at it — "moved this turn" is still true, so it's a legal target and the spell doesn't fizzle on targeting — it just resolves and the move does nothing. Hunker Down also being [Reaction] means you can play it in response to the Siren's Song itself and it will resolve first.

Two caveats worth knowing: this blocks every kind of move (Standard Move, Showstopper, Ride the Wind, Siren's Song), since the restriction doesn't care who is doing the moving — but it does not stop a Recall, because a Recall isn't a Move (Rule 448.1). Also, nothing else about the unit is affected: it's still a legal target for kill/damage effects, and it's already readied by Hunker Down.

question: If I have a Mageseeker Warden at a battlefield, and then play Firebrand Raider does Mageseeker Warden's "can't" effect stop the enemy units from getting ready when Firebrand Raider enters, and also stop the enemies units from entering ready
answer:
Partly — the "ready all enemy units" trigger gets shut off, but the "enter ready" part isn't affected at all.

Mageseeker Warden is a static prohibition: spells and abilities can't ready units that are enemy to its controller. Since you control both Warden and Firebrand Raider, the opponent's units are enemy units to you, so Firebrand Raider's "When you play me, ready all enemy units" ability does nothing while Warden is at a battlefield — it can't flip exhausted enemy units back to ready. But "Other units enter ready" is not a readying action: units arrive already ready and are never seen as exhausted, so Warden can't touch it — same reasoning as Accelerate, Sun Disc, and "I enter ready" units (FAQ #2897, #4300). So your opponent's fresh units still enter ready, and Firebrand Raider's own "I enter ready" applies normally.

Two follow-on notes: Firebrand Raider's "Units don't ready during the Awaken Phase" is a restriction, not an ability that readies anything, so Warden doesn't interfere with it — nobody readies in the Awaken Phase while Firebrand Raider is in play. And Warden's other clause only limits where opponents can play units, so it doesn't restrict you playing Firebrand Raider to a battlefield.
