question: If I am playing Volibear legend, and I play Seraphic Wyvern. Volibear legend triggers and Seraphic Wyvern trigger, Does the 1 rune channels ready plus 1 rune exhausted, or are both runes channelled exhausted?
answer:
No — both runes enter exhausted, not one ready plus one exhausted.

Volibear's ability generates a channel event that already carries the "exhausted" stipulation, and Seraphic Wyvern's replacement inherits modifications from the effect that generated the event (Rule 375 — same as its Gold-token example, where the additional token also enters exhausted). So Volibear's "channel 1 rune exhausted" becomes "channel 2 runes, both exhausted": you get the base rune exhausted and Seraphic Wyvern's extra rune exhausted, total 2 runes with none ready.

The one thing to watch is that Seraphic Wyvern must still be on the board when Volibear's trigger resolves (channeling happens on resolution, not at trigger) — if your opponent kills it in response, you're back to just 1 exhausted rune.

question: si je joue Tideturner et je veux échanger sa place avec un Reckless Innovator déjà exhaust, est ce que je fais un gold ?
answer:
Non — échanger les positions avec Tideturner ne fait pas « devenir exhausted » le Reckless Innovator, donc aucun jeton Gold n'est créé.

L'abilité de Reckless Innovator se déclenche sur « When I become exhausted », donc il doit passer de ready à exhausté. Ici il est déjà exhausté : une unité déjà exhaustée ne peut pas l'être de nouveau (règle 415.1.b), et le swap de Tideturner n'est qu'un Move entre deux locations (règles 421 / 448), pas une exhaustion — donc le déclencheur ne se lève jamais.

Pour obtenir le Gold, il faut que l'Innovator soit ready au moment où il s'exhauste (attaque, Standard Move, ou exhaustion comme coût). Note aussi que si tu le joues avec Accelerate il entre ready — mais ce n'est pas le cas ici.

question: If I kill a bomb token with the additional cost of playing Shimmering Swimmer, would the bombs deathknell and the Swimmer's when played trigger go on the chain simultaneously?
answer:
Yes — if you kill your own Bomb token as the additional cost for Shimmering Swimmer, the Bomb's Deathknell and the Swimmer's "when you play me" trigger are placed on the chain simultaneously, and since you control both you choose the order they go on (Rule 383.3.d; FAQ #6068). The Swimmer resolves fully and enters play first, then both triggers are queued together — that's the standard "additional cost kills a friendly permanent" timing.

The Bomb is a gear token, but tokens can have and trigger Deathknell just fine (Rule 808.1.d), so nothing there changes. Note the Bomb's ability is not optional and not friendly: it deals 2 to an enemy unit "here" and kills your other Bombs at that location — "here" is locked in at the Bomb's old location, where the Swimmer isn't (it enters at your Base or a battlefield you control). The Swimmer's half deals 2 to a unit of your choice, so it can hit that same enemy unit or anything else.

Whichever went on the chain last resolves first; if you want the Swimmer's 2 damage to finish off a unit the Bomb also damaged, order accordingly.

question: When a Reflection token created by conquering a unit with Deceiver's reflexive ability is moved to base before the copy effect resolves, does the copy still succeed if only the token moves to base, versus if both the token and the target unit are moved to base?
answer:
Yes — the copy still works if only the Reflection token moves to base; it fails only if the target unit is no longer at that battlefield.

Deceiver's reflexive trigger targets "another unit there," and that's the only thing with a location restriction. The token itself is not a target of the trigger — it's the object being modified ("It becomes a copy of…"), and moving to Base isn't a zone change, so it's still the same game object the copy effect applies to wherever it sits. Mirror Image proves the point: it makes the token at your Base copy a unit that can be at a battlefield, so the copy never requires co-location.

If the target unit is what moves to Base, the instruction mistargets — no unit matching "another unit there" — so the token stays a 0 [M] Reflection (and still gets Temporary, since that instruction doesn't depend on the target). Rule 359.3.e.9; copy effects are just a layer application (479.1), and the token keeps its token nature regardless.

question: i have a hidden temporal breach on battlefield with my nasus. opponent plays charm to move my nasus. i play the hidden temporal breach to target my nasus. will the charm still move my nasus?
answer:
Yes — Charm fizzles and Nasus stays put.

Your hidden Temporal Breach has Reaction (assuming it was hidden on an earlier turn), so you play it in response to Charm, targeting Nasus at the battlefield where it was hidden — legal, since Hidden only restricts targets to that battlefield. Breach banishes Nasus and its owner replays him to the same location as a brand-new game object, so Charm's target has changed zones to and from a non-board zone and is no longer legal. Charm resolves with no effect: nothing moves (Rule 359.3.e.4).

Two small notes: Nasus comes back exhausted, but he's still there so you keep the battlefield. And you must fire the Breach while Charm is on the chain — if you let Charm resolve first, you lose the unit and the cleanup that follows trashes the hidden card. (If that's Nasus, Ascended, Charm's caster also has to pay 2 extra any-domain power for Deflect 2 just to target him.)

question: If i exhaust my Riven, Broken Blade with my Ki Burst does Ki Burst or Riven, Broken Blade ability resolves first ?
answer:
Riven's ability resolves first. Exhausting her is the additional cost to play Ki Burst, and that happens while Ki Burst is still being played — anything that triggers during the process of playing a spell goes on the chain above it and resolves before the spell does (FAQ #4103). So Riven's "When I become exhausted" trigger finalizes and resolves, then Ki Burst resolves and Stuns its target.

So the ordering matters in your favor: you can pick the "spend my buff to ready me" mode and she'll be ready again before Ki Burst finishes — the exhaust was already paid as a cost, so readying her doesn't undo or fizzle the spell. Just note the Stun and ready modes require her to already have a buff to spend; otherwise the Buff mode is your line.

One thing to watch: Ki Burst's Stun target is chosen when you play the spell, so Riven's trigger resolving first can't change what Ki Burst is pointed at.

question: what if i pass focus
answer:
Yes — passing Focus hands Focus and Priority to your opponent, and it doesn't end the Showdown unless they pass too (Rule 348).

They can play an Action or Reaction, activate an ability, or pass back. If they play something, you don't get your "pass" back — once that chain resolves and the state returns to Open, Focus automatically moves to the next player in turn order (Rule 346), so the Showdown keeps going as long as anyone acts. Note the pass that matters is the Pass action with an empty chain, not passing Priority mid-chain (Rule 347.2.a).

Once you both pass in sequence, it's a Combat Showdown → Combat Damage, then Combat Cleanup (which heals all units). A Non-Combat Showdown has no damage step or healing — if only one player's units remain, they establish Control and Conquer if they haven't scored there this turn.

question: Can you play an Ambush unit such as Rengar, Trophy Hunter in reaction to Mageseeker Warden entering the battlefield?
answer:
Yes — you can Ambush in response to Mageseeker Warden being played, because at that moment Warden is a card on the chain, not yet a permanent on the board.

Warden's "opponents can only play units to their base" is a passive ability of a permanent, and passive abilities are only active while the permanent is on the board (Rule 365.1). So while Warden sits on the chain, you're free to Ambush a unit (Rengar included) to a battlefield you control — or, for Rengar, a battlefield with enemy units — and your unit resolves first (LIFO), landing before Warden ever enters.

The window that matters is after Warden resolves: once it's actually at a battlefield, no Ambush for you at any battlefield, and you're limited to playing units to your base. Note it's a restriction on playing, not on units already there, so your Ambush unit that landed earlier stays put. If Warden is played to its controller's base, the clause never turns on at all.

question: Star Spring
answer:
It depends on the scenario you're asking about, but the core ruling: Star Spring triggers once per player each turn, not once total — the first time each player plays a non-token unit there, that player may move another unit they control at Star Spring back to its base.

Three things people get wrong: only an actual play counts (moving a unit in does not use up or trigger the first-time condition), tokens never trigger it, and a unit that enters via a replacement effect never "enters here" — e.g. Baron Nashor played to Star Spring goes to Baron Pit instead, so no trigger (Rule 369.3, FAQ #12852).

question: If you hidden blade opponent unit and they sacrifice it how many cards they draw
answer:
No — they draw 0 cards from your Hidden Blade. Their own kill/sacrifice removes the unit before Hidden Blade resolves, so Hidden Blade mistargets: the "Kill a unit at a battlefield" instruction is ignored, and since the draw is a linked instruction to it, "Its controller draws 2" is ignored too (CR 359.3.e.14.a; FAQ #3700).

The exception is if the "sacrifice" is actually a replacement effect that keeps the unit on the battlefield (Zhonya's Hourglass, Sett legend). Then the unit is still a legal target at a battlefield when Hidden Blade resolves, so its controller still draws 2 even though the kill was replaced (FAQ #6894).

question:
When Ziggs, Explosive decks pile lots of bombs on one battlefield, and they are detonated (let's say 4 bombs), does every single bomb have to pay deflect cost?

All of my online opponents, especially Irelias, are trying to make me pay the deflect for every single bomb (so 4 bombs = 4 recycled for deflect 1).
answer:
Yes — each Bomb is its own object with its own death trigger, so 4 Bombs detonating means 4 separate triggered abilities, and every one of them that chooses a unit with Deflect carries its own Deflect cost (Rule 809.1.c: the cost is paid "for each time they choose me"). If all four pick the Irelia, that's Deflect ×4 — your opponents have that part right.

But they're leaving out your out: Deflect is a mandatory cost for spells, while for triggered abilities you choose targets, then at finalization you may simply decline to pay, and that trigger is removed from the chain with no effect at all (Rule 405.2; FAQ #10636). So you pay for as many or as few of the four as you want — no one can force you to pay for all of them. Two things to keep straight: declining kills the whole trigger, so if the Bomb you decline was the one whose trigger would "kill your other Bombs there," that chain reaction stops too; and if there's a non-Deflect enemy unit at that battlefield, choosing it costs you nothing. Also, Deflect power can be paid with any domain (Rule 809.1.c.1), so don't let anyone insist it must match something.

question: When a unit gains the Attacker designation mid-combat through an effect like Nidalee, Cat Form's Ambush, does Demacian Standard's attack trigger fire again for that newly attacking unit?
answer:
Yes — Demacian Standard's ability is an attack trigger, so it fires again for the new attacker.

Standard reads "When one or more friendly units attack here, give one of them +2 [M] this turn." That's keyed to the Attacker designation, not to combat starting (Rule 383.4.e), so Nidalee ambushing to that battlefield and gaining the Attacker designation during the following Cleanup is a fresh trigger event — you get another +2 [M] to hand out, on top of whatever the Standard already gave earlier in this combat.

What limits it is per-unit, not per-combat: Attack triggers are only checked the first time each unit gains the Attacker designation in a given combat (Rule 383.4.e.2.a). So bouncing Nidalee out and replaying her, or re-designating the same unit, won't re-fire it — but a genuinely new attacker will.

One caveat: this only works if it's a real Combat Showdown. If Nidalee were played to a battlefield with no enemy units, no Attacker designation is ever granted, so nothing triggers.

question: I use Ekko to play Clocktower Guardian with discount. He dies at the end of the turn and I have a time warp on the top of my deck. What happens?
answer:
Yes — the kill and the Deathknell both resolve before your turn actually ends, so you banish the Time Warp, you may play it right then, and you take the extra turn after this one.

The "Kill me at end of turn" from Boy Who Shattered Time happens in the Ending Step (Rule 317.1), which is before the Expiration Step, so your rune pool hasn't emptied yet (317.2.d) — anything still floating in it is usable for the play. Clocktower Guardian's Deathknell then banishes Time Warp and lets you play it as part of that resolution (same as the combat case in FAQ #12960 — no Open State needed), and "play it" isn't restricted to units, so a spell is fine.

The catch is that the discount only ignores the Energy cost, not Power. Time Warp is 10 Energy / 4 Mind power, so you still need 4 Mind power from ready Mind runes or unspent pool. If you can't pay it, the Time Warp just stays in Banishment — the permission is spent with that resolution, so it doesn't sit around to be played later. If you do pay, Time Warp resolves, banishes itself, and the additional turn is inserted right after your current turn (Rule 738), so you take it before the next player's turn.

question: How does focus priority work when playing a Rengar, Trophy Hunter
answer:
It depends on whose focus window you're in when he hits the table — Rengar is a [Reaction] play (his Ambush lets him go to a battlefield with enemy units even if you have none there), so you can only play him when you hold focus in a Showdown Open State or priority on an existing chain (Rule 347.1). Once his chain item closes and the turn returns to Open, focus moves to the next player in turn order (Rule 346), so you can't play him and then immediately start another chain — your opponent gets first crack.

Two things people usually get wrong here. First, nobody can respond to Rengar being played: units finalize and enter play immediately during the Finalize step (Rule 337.2), so there's no reaction window to the play itself — only triggered abilities (a "when you play me," "when a unit enters here," etc.) go on the chain and can be responded to.

Second, playing him doesn't earn you focus or make you the attacker. The player who applied Contested keeps the Attacker designation and the opening focus (Rule 345); Rengar entering a battlefield you don't control makes you the Defender (FAQ #10056), and any Shield/Assault only matter once combat actually begins. If combat has already started, the combat chain opened from triggered abilities, so focus does not pass when that chain empties (Rule 346.1).

question: Zhonya's Hourglass dies as a unit gear, will Zhonya's Hourglass see itself and recall
answer:
No — a Zhonya's Hourglass that's been turned into a unit gear (e.g. via Lady of Clockwork) does not save itself when it dies.

It does "see" its own death: while it's a unit gear it's a friendly unit, so its replacement effect applies to its own death — Rule 370.2's example literally has a gear-unit Hourglass's effect applying to its own death. But the applied effect is "kill this instead," so the Hourglass gets killed, which is the death that was already happening. The "heal that unit, exhaust it, and recall it" then has nothing to reach, because the Hourglass is in the trash rather than on the board, and a replacement effect can't be applied twice to the same death (Rule 370.2).

The self-save only works with two copies: the second Hourglass's effect replaces the kill of the first (Rule 370.2), so one survives and the one whose effect is applied last is the one that dies — you pick that order. None of this uses the chain; replacement effects apply on their own.

question: If opponent play a card and i react with a card that play Brynhir. when the chain resolve does opponent card effect resolve?
answer:
Yes — the opponent's card still resolves. Brynhir only stops new plays; anything already on the chain finishes resolving regardless of her.

One detail on sequencing: Brynhir's "When you play me" trigger goes on the chain above the opponent's card, so it resolves first and locks them out of playing anything further that turn — but their original card then resolves normally. They also get a chance to respond while her trigger is on the chain, before it applies (FAQ 3849).

question: if i play Baron in a controlled battlefield and my legend is riven The Exile. Did Baron creat the Pit AND enters ready?
answer:
Yes — you get both. Baron's "add the Baron Pit if it's not there already, if you do I enter there" and The Exile's "units you play to battlefields you control enter ready" are both replacement effects that apply to the same enter-the-board event, so as the controller of Baron you choose the order they apply (CR 372, CR 369.3).

Order them so the ready one resolves first and then the Pit relocation: the relocation only rewrites where he enters, it doesn't change the state he enters in. Riven's effect keys off where he was played to (a battlefield you control), which is true, so he still enters ready even though he ends up in the Pit.

Note the Pit arrives uncontrolled, so it becomes Contested and you'll go through a Non-Combat Showdown, then Conquer the Pit after it ends (assuming you haven't already scored it that turn). The one way to miss it: playing him somewhere other than a battlefield you control, e.g. to your Base — then The Exile's condition isn't met and he enters exhausted.

question: Can i replay Dancing Grenade when played with Fizz, Trickster after it got recycled?
answer:
No — once Fizz's recycle replaces the trip to the trash, Dancing Grenade is on the bottom of your deck, and its "play this spell again for [A]" permission only works from the trash.

Fizz's "Then recycle it" is a replacement effect that applies whenever the spell would leave the chain, for any reason — it isn't optional and it doesn't leave you a trashed copy (FAQ #10401). So when Dancing Grenade resolves, the card goes straight to the bottom of the deck instead of the trash, and the recast instruction (which the damaged unit's controller gains) has no card to find.

Worth flagging: the controller who gets the recast option is the controller of the unit that took the 2 damage, not necessarily you — but it doesn't matter here, because the card never lands in anyone's trash. Played normally (not via Fizz), the loop works as usual.

question: When i play a dockside Dockside Lock-Up and use the jarvan trigger to move nidalee in - do i initiate a combat showdown to draw with Nidalee, Cat Form
answer:
It depends on whether enemy units are still there after Dockside's own trigger resolves — with a lone enemy unit there, no combat happens and Nidalee doesn't draw.

You never "initiate" a Combat Showdown; it's staged automatically in a Cleanup, and only once the Chain is empty (Rule 462). Both Dockside Lock-Up's play trigger ("banish a unit here") and Jarvan's move trigger fire off the same event and sit on the Chain together, so both resolve before any combat can open — you choose the order (Rule 383.3.d), but that doesn't save it. With one enemy unit there, it gets banished as the Chain resolves, Nidalee then arrives at a battlefield you don't control with no enemy units present, so you get a Non-Combat Showdown and a Conquer — no combat, no "win a combat," no draw.

If a second enemy unit is still there after the banish, Nidalee arrives with defenders present, Combat is staged, she's the Attacker (she applied Contested) and she draws only if she remains after combat — if she trades and dies, no draw (she isn't present to evaluate the win condition).

question: if you play the back off spell card hidden do you still draw one?
answer:
No — playing Back Off from hidden doesn't draw you a card, because its draw is conditional on playing it from your hand, and a card played from facedown isn't played from hand.

You still get the Stun effect (it resolves at its cost of [0] once played from hidden, gaining Reaction). One restriction to remember: because it's played from facedown, the unit you Stun must be chosen from among units at the battlefield where you hid Back Off, unless another effect loosens that (Rule 811.1.d.2).
